question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Seoul, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

notes.anthropic: Korea's most internationally connected gallery since 1982; represents Lee Ufan, Haegue Yang, Anish Kapoor and blue-chip Western estates, with a heavy Frieze/Art Basel presence.
notes.openai: Korea’s leading international gallery, with a blue-chip programme, major institutional reach and decades of Art Basel participation.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1970, the oldest contemporary gallery in Korea; steward of Park Soo-keun, Kim Whanki, Nam June Paik and Lee Kun-Yong legacies alongside a strong younger programme.
notes.openai: Founded in 1970, it helped build Korea’s modern gallery system and remains central to Dansaekhwa and contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Rigorous programme built around Yun Hyong-keun, Suh Se Ok, Olafur Eliasson and Cody Choi; a key driver of Dansaekhwa-era reappraisal abroad.
notes.openai: A highly respected Korean gallery with a rigorous international programme and sustained institutional and art-fair visibility.

notes.anthropic: First mega-gallery to commit to Seoul (2017, expanded 2021); anchors the Hannam gallery cluster with Yoshitomo Nara, Lee Kun-Yong and Pace's global roster.
notes.openai: The Seoul branch of a global blue-chip gallery, presenting major international and Korean artists in museum-scale exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: In Seoul since 2017 in a SO-IL-designed space; long-running commitment to Do Ho Suh, Lee Bul, Sung Neung Kyung and Kim Yun Shin.
notes.openai: Longstanding Seoul outpost of an influential international gallery with an especially strong Korean and Asian programme.

notes.anthropic: Opened 2021 with museum-scale shows of Baselitz, Rauschenberg and Han Bing; central to Seoul's post-Frieze internationalisation.
notes.openai: Ambitious Seoul space for one of Europe’s most powerful galleries, regularly mounting historically significant exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Collector-founded gallery with a pan-Asian roster (Korea, China, India, Southeast Asia) and an appetite for difficult, research-driven work.
notes.openai: An influential Korean gallery and collecting enterprise with a strong record of developing major Asian contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Since 1988 a bridge between Korean modernism, minjung art and contemporary practice; strong scholarly exhibitions and international fair presence.
notes.openai: Important for connecting Korean art history, Dansaekhwa and contemporary practice through a sustained scholarly programme.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1983; large Pyeongchang-dong complex plus Hannam and Nine One spaces, historically decisive for Korean modern and minjung art markets.
notes.openai: One of Korea’s largest and longest-running commercial galleries, with significant domestic infrastructure and fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Early international arrival (2016) plus a Dosan Park space; blends global names with Korean artists such as Park Seo-Bo's late estate context and Bae Hyung-Kyung.
notes.openai: A prominent branch of the global gallery, combining internationally recognizable artists with an active Korean programme.

notes.anthropic: Seoul's most influential noncommercial kunsthalle since 1998; launched careers of Korean artists later shown at Venice and Documenta.
notes.openai: A foundational Korean contemporary-art institution known for influential commissions, exhibitions and curatorial experimentation.

notes.anthropic: Opened 2021, bringing Anicka Yi, Alex Katz and Ugo Rondinone shows to Gangnam and legitimising Cheongdam as an international gallery district.
notes.openai: Permanent Seoul branch of a major international gallery known for critically established and museum-level artists.

notes.anthropic: Berlin gallery's Seoul outpost brings conceptual and installation-led practices (Philippe Parreno, Ryan Gander, Ann Veronica Janssens) to Korean audiences.
notes.openai: Seoul branch of the conceptually driven Berlin gallery, representing many institutionally prominent international artists.

notes.anthropic: Foundation space in a Herzog & de Meuron building; its SongEun Art Award has been a career-making platform for emerging Korean artists since 2001.
notes.openai: A major nonprofit platform with an architecturally distinguished space, ambitious exhibitions and longstanding support for emerging Korean artists.

notes.anthropic: The leading gallery of Korea's mid-career generation — Park Kyung-ryul, Jung Heeseung, Kang Seung Lee, Haneyl Choi — with consistent international fair placement.
notes.openai: A key advocate for Korean contemporary artists, with sustained international art-fair participation and curatorial credibility.

notes.anthropic: Sharp, design-literate programme mixing Korean artists with European names; a fixture at Frieze, Art Basel and Liste.
notes.openai: Respected for a sharply edited international programme and for introducing emerging and mid-career artists to Korea.

notes.anthropic: Young dealer with outsized international profile, showing Urs Fischer, Sarah Lucas and Ella Kruglyanskaya in Seoul.
notes.openai: A closely watched Korean gallery whose concentrated programme has rapidly gained international critical and fair visibility.

notes.anthropic: Beijing/Hong Kong gallery's Seoul branch, one of the few venues consistently showing major Chinese contemporary artists in Korea.
notes.openai: The Seoul branch of a major Asian gallery network, with a broad programme and substantial regional art-fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Busan's leading gallery (Lee Bae, Kim Chong Hak) with a permanent Seoul space and a strong Frieze Seoul and international fair record.
notes.openai: The Seoul presence of a distinguished Korean gallery especially important to Dansaekhwa, abstraction and Busan’s art history.

notes.anthropic: Lean, curatorially serious gallery with Korean and international emerging artists; regular at Liste and Frieze Seoul.
notes.openai: Influential compact gallery known for discovering younger Korean artists and placing them in wider international conversations.

notes.anthropic: Contemporary arm of the antiquities dealer; ambitious curated shows of international mid-career artists and strong institutional collaborations.
notes.openai: Known for ambitious exhibitions by internationally active artists addressing history, politics and cross-cultural exchange.

notes.anthropic: Corporate-funded, curator-led space whose Hermès Foundation Missulsang has been one of Korea's most prestigious art prizes.
notes.openai: A longstanding Fondation d’entreprise Hermès exhibition space with serious commissions and support for Korean contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Critically respected small gallery representing young Korean artists with a conceptual, materially inventive bent.
notes.openai: One of Seoul’s most closely followed younger galleries, with an experimental programme and growing international fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Doosan Art Center's gallery and its residency/award pipeline in Seoul and New York are a key incubator for artists under 40.
notes.openai: Important corporate nonprofit supporting emerging artists and curators through exhibitions, awards and an international residency network.

notes.anthropic: Long-running gallery with Palpan-dong and Pyeongchang-dong spaces, known for backing experimental Korean painters early.
notes.openai: A respected Korean gallery recognized for sustained relationships with distinctive emerging and mid-career artists.

notes.anthropic: Daegu-founded gallery with a permanent Seoul space; solid Korean modern-contemporary crossovers and international fair activity.
notes.openai: Established Korean gallery with strong postwar and contemporary rosters and regular participation in international fairs.

notes.anthropic: Founded 2021 by veteran dealers; museum-quality shows of Korean artists including Kim Beom-adjacent conceptual practices.
notes.openai: A curatorially focused gallery representing conceptually rigorous Korean and international contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Korea's first alternative space (1999), a foundational platform for media, performance and Asian curatorial exchange.
notes.openai: One of Korea’s pioneering alternative spaces, active since the 1990s and important to experimental and socially engaged art.

notes.anthropic: Long-running Samcheong gallery with an experimental, artist-friendly programme and open-call exhibitions.
notes.openai: Long-running gallery with a critically engaged programme spanning experimental younger artists and established Korean figures.

notes.anthropic: Design-inflected Cheongdam gallery bringing European contemporary artists to Korean collectors.
notes.openai: Established contemporary gallery with an international roster and consistent participation in major Korean and overseas fairs.

notes.anthropic: Hybrid gallery/project space known for rigorous curatorial framing of emerging Korean artists and criticism-led programming.
notes.openai: A longstanding curatorial gallery and incubator that has helped establish numerous emerging Korean artists.

notes.anthropic: LA gallery whose 2019 Seoul space was an early bet on the city; strong diasporic Korean-American and emerging international programme.
notes.openai: The Seoul branch of the US gallery, notable for trans-Pacific programming and support of emerging international practices.

notes.anthropic: Early mover in Seongsu; contemporary programme of Korean and international emerging artists across multiple spaces.
notes.openai: Combines exhibitions, residencies and production support, providing meaningful long-term development for contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Kolon-funded nonprofit in a Mass Studies-designed building; free, well-produced solo shows by Korean and international artists.
notes.openai: Kolon’s nonprofit art space, mounting substantial exhibitions by major Korean and international contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Tokyo gallery's Kengo Kuma-designed Seoul space; Gutai and postwar Japanese material alongside contemporary Asian painting.
notes.openai: Large Seoul branch of an established Asian gallery network, with substantial exhibitions and broad regional market reach.

notes.anthropic: Fast-rising young gallery with two Seoul spaces; a bellwether for the post-2020 emerging Korean scene.
notes.openai: A young gallery with a focused programme that has quickly attracted curatorial attention and international fair exposure.
The Seoul branch of the internationally influential London-founded gallery, with a major global artist roster.

notes.anthropic: Small, critically attentive gallery for emerging Korean and international artists, active at young-gallery fairs.
notes.openai: An artist-centered independent venue known for adventurous exhibitions by younger Korean and international practitioners.

notes.anthropic: Seochon mainstay showing Korean conceptual and media artists; a steady presence at domestic fairs since the 1990s.
notes.openai: Respected for its longevity and carefully developed programme of Korean and international contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Euljiro project space combining exhibitions with critical writing and publishing on emerging practice.
notes.openai: An influential independent platform for experimental exhibitions, emerging practices and curator-led projects.

notes.anthropic: Youth-oriented gallery that helped launch a generation of Korean painters now on the international fair circuit.
notes.openai: A lively younger gallery advancing emerging Korean artists through closely curated exhibitions and international fairs.

notes.anthropic: Historic alternative space and publisher with a politically engaged, discourse-driven programme since 1999.
notes.openai: Historically central to Korea’s alternative-space movement, with a critical, research-oriented and socially engaged programme.

notes.anthropic: Veteran gallery (est. 1983) with a strong Korean modern and abstract painting programme.
notes.openai: An established Seoul gallery with a broad contemporary roster and consistent presence in Korea’s commercial art scene.

notes.anthropic: Architecturally striking Hannam space with a tightly curated contemporary programme.
notes.openai: A respected independent venue offering emerging artists room for installation-led and materially experimental projects.
The Seoul outpost of a highly influential gallery known for conceptually rigorous, historically important artists.
A global blue-chip gallery presenting prominent postwar and contemporary artists in its permanent Seoul space.
Internationally respected for a cross-generational, research-led programme connecting Latin America, Europe and Asia.

notes.anthropic: Daegu gallery (est. 1992) with a Seoul space; Korean postwar experimental art and international minimal/conceptual figures.
notes.openai: Seoul branch of the important Daegu gallery, extending its respected programme of abstraction and contemporary practice.
The Seoul space of the influential Italian gallery, bringing a strong international roster into dialogue with the Korean market.

notes.anthropic: Well-funded exhibition space opened 2022 with ambitious curated group shows of international contemporary art.
notes.openai: A large contemporary venue known for polished presentations of internationally active artists and ambitious collaborations.

notes.anthropic: Focused programme of Korean and Japanese contemporary artists with careful, restrained installations.
notes.openai: A well-regarded younger gallery presenting distinctive Korean artists and increasingly visible international collaborations.

notes.anthropic: Small Euljiro space typical of the district's DIY scene, showing young artists and design-art crossovers.
notes.openai: A critically regarded independent space emphasizing close artist collaboration, experimentation and emerging practices.

notes.anthropic: Former inn turned cultural complex with galleries, residencies and publishing; a hub of Seochon's art community.
notes.openai: A historically resonant multidisciplinary venue supporting experimental exhibitions, residencies and independent cultural production.

notes.anthropic: Curator-run space with research-heavy exhibitions and a reputation for spotting artists before institutions do.
notes.openai: A curator-run collective space influential in Seoul’s experimental scene and discourse around exhibition-making.

notes.anthropic: Berlin gallery's Asian base since 2022, showing market-forward painting and a young international roster to Seoul collectors.
Long-established Samcheong gallery with a quiet, connoisseurial programme of Korean modern and contemporary art.
notes.openai: Long-established gallery associated with Korean abstraction, postwar art and a stable programme of contemporary artists.
A formative public platform for emerging Korean artists and independent curatorial practice.
A pioneering artist-support organization whose exhibitions and grants have shaped several generations of Korean contemporary art.
A private nonprofit presenting contemporary exhibitions, performances and commissions in a major purpose-built complex.

notes.anthropic: Quietly influential Samcheong gallery pairing established Korean conceptualists with strong younger sculptors and painters.
Long-standing gallery with Korea-Japan exchange exhibitions and a Heyri satellite.
notes.openai: An established Korean gallery with decades of activity, international partnerships and regular art-fair participation.

notes.anthropic: Seongsu gallery with a strong Korean abstraction and international mid-career programme in a large industrial space.
notes.openai: Prominent Gangnam gallery presenting established Korean and international artists and participating actively in major fairs.
Independent nonprofit known for research-led exhibitions, open calls and sustained support of emerging artists and curators.

notes.anthropic: Cheongdam gallery known for photography and media-based Korean artists.
notes.openai: Known for supporting emerging and mid-career Korean artists through polished exhibitions and sustained market development.
Despite its name, an independent project space recognized for conceptually ambitious exhibitions and artist-led experimentation.
A small but closely watched space with a critically engaged programme of emerging Korean and international artists.

notes.anthropic: Dedicated photography gallery supporting emerging photographers through consistent solo exhibitions.
notes.openai: One of Seoul’s longstanding specialist photography galleries, important to the development of Korea’s photographic art market.

notes.anthropic: Nonprofit with influential awards for artists and art critics, supporting research-based practice outside the market.

notes.openai: An artist-focused space valued for intimate exhibitions, experimentation and attention to process and drawing broadly understood.
An established Korean gallery with a stable roster, strong collector relationships and regular domestic fair participation.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1983; pioneering in introducing international contemporary artists to Seoul and supporting Korean sculptors.
One of Insadong's oldest galleries, a barometer of the traditional Korean art trade with regular contemporary shows.
notes.openai: A historically important Insa-dong gallery with exceptional longevity and longstanding support for Korean contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Insadong institution since 1977; historically important for Korean modern painting and Sun Contemporary's younger arm.

notes.openai: A long-running Korean gallery with significant historical involvement in promoting Korean postwar and contemporary art abroad.

notes.anthropic: Contemporary gallery known for design-conscious installations and emerging Korean artists since the mid-2000s.

notes.openai: An active contemporary gallery with multiple generations of artists and a visible Korean and regional fair programme.
An internationally oriented space presenting experimental and conceptually driven artists in a cross-regional programme.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run Mapo space known for feminist and queer-inflected programming and emerging artists' first solos.
notes.openai: A significant artist-run venue in Seoul’s independent ecosystem, known for emerging artists and self-organized programming.

notes.anthropic: Converted post office running interdisciplinary exhibitions, performance and discourse programmes.
notes.openai: An artist-run former post office that became an important site for experimental exhibitions and independent collaborations.

notes.anthropic: Cologne-Seoul gallery introducing European emerging artists to Korea and Korean artists to Germany.

notes.openai: Permanent Seoul space of the Portuguese gallery, bringing an internationally emerging roster into the local ecosystem.

notes.anthropic: Popular Seongsu gallery for young figurative painters and illustration-adjacent contemporary art, with a large collector following.
notes.openai: A recognizable younger gallery whose accessible but focused programme connects Korean artists with wider Asian audiences.

notes.anthropic: Established Gangnam gallery with a Korean modern and contemporary painting programme and deep collector base.
notes.openai: A veteran Gangnam gallery with substantial longevity and a programme spanning Korean and international contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Photography-focused gallery that has been central to the market for contemporary Korean photography.

notes.openai: The Seoul base of a Korean-American gallery connecting artists and institutions across Korea and the United States.
A curator-led nonprofit supporting emerging practices through exhibitions, research and sustained critical exchange.

Free exhibition space atop the Frank Gehry-designed Maison, presenting Fondation Louis Vuitton collection works.

An emerging gallery noted for experimental presentations and a programme attentive to younger Korean practices.

notes.openai: A long-running contemporary gallery that has consistently introduced and supported emerging Korean artists.
A young Seoul-and-Cologne gallery building international visibility through emerging artists and selective fair participation.
An internationally oriented emerging gallery whose Seoul programme links younger practices across Europe and Asia.

notes.anthropic: Idiosyncratic artist-run space in a hanok alley, influential in Seoul's small-scale experimental scene.

notes.openai: A respected photography-focused gallery that has presented important Korean and international image-based artists.

notes.anthropic: Independent space in central Seoul mixing exhibitions, performance and publishing for a younger audience.
notes.openai: A developing independent venue offering space for experimental exhibitions and new curatorial voices.
Active commercial gallery supporting Korean artists through exhibitions, publications and regular domestic art-fair participation.
A contemporary gallery with a consistent emerging-artist programme and growing visibility in Korea’s fair circuit.
An established venue particularly notable for contemporary photography and lens-based exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Corporate-run underground exhibition hall commissioning large-scale installations by international artists.

notes.openai: A polished exhibition platform connected to Noblesse magazine, presenting established and emerging contemporary artists.
A durable independent venue combining contemporary art, design and publishing through collaborative, process-oriented projects.

Contemporary gallery with a design and craft-adjacent programme and consistent emerging-artist solos.

A new large-scale contemporary-art venue in Bukchon designed for ambitious commissions and interdisciplinary exhibitions.

Long-running Jongno gallery with a steady programme of Korean painters and sculptors.
